transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan P., Leah K., Marcus O. (Redwood) -- Priya R., Daniel C., Samantha L. (Alpine Fintech)

Summary:
This is a POC scoping kickoff focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for Alpine's financial doc summarization product. Primary goals: define success criteria (latency, cost, quality), gather workload signature (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), and align on benchmarks and timeline for a 3-week pilot. Customer emphasized strict security (KMS + SSO) and a preference for private deployment if latency/cost tradeoffs require it.

Topics covered:
- Current prod traffic shape and pain points
- Target SLAs (p95 latency, throughput) and cost objectives
- Representative prompt/profile collection and token distributions
- Benchmark plan: steady, burst, and long-tail tests
- Private vs dedicated vs hosted decision drivers
- Next steps and responsible owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: All right, thanks everyone for hopping on. Quick intros, and then we'll jump to the workload profile.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here - head of ML at Alpine. We run a doc summarization pipeline used by our loan ops team. Latency is visible in the UI so it matters a lot.
[00:21] Daniel Cho: Daniel, platform. We'll own the infra pieces — traffic shaping, autoscaling, that side.
[00:26] Samantha Li: Samantha, security. I have questions about keys, audit logs, and retention.
[00:31] Jordan Patel: Great. Leah, Marcus, quick bios?
[00:34] Leah Kim: Leah, I lead SE for inference; I focus on throughput, batching, and token-level cost.
[00:38] Marcus Ortega: Marcus here — typically run our bench harness and help with KV cache and quantization guidance.
[00:44] Jordan Patel: Cool. Priya, can you describe the current traffic shape? QPS, peak behavior?
[00:50] Priya Rao: Sure. Baseline steady is small — around 80 to 120 QPS during business hours. But we see big bursts tied to nightly batch jobs and onboarding events. Peak bursts can hit ~1,100 to 1,300 QPS for short windows, like 3 to 8 minutes. Concurrency at the model layer today is spotty — we run on a mix of pods and managed endpoints.
[01:14] Leah Kim: That's helpful. Do you have a token mix? Average input length, expected generated length?
[01:19] Priya Rao: We parsed logs. Median input tokens ~42, 75th ~90. Generated tokens vary: median 120, 95th 420 for long case notes. Most important is 99th percentile— those long narratives blow up cost.
[01:33] Marcus Ortega: Does that include any multi-turn context? Are you appending history?
[01:37] Priya Rao: We keep a short history per user, usually 1 previous exchange, adds ~18 tokens on average. So total input often 60-ish.
[01:45] Daniel Cho: For concurrency, our app holds open ~250 websocket clients during peaks, but not all call the model simultaneously. At model side we see bursts of 200-400 concurrent requests commonly, with spikes up to 800 in a collapse scenario.
[02:01] Jordan Patel: OK, so rough target for the POC — what would success look like?
[02:05] Priya Rao: Three things: p95 generation latency under 600ms for requests up to 256 output tokens, cost per 1k tokens under our internal target (we gave a threshold in the RFP), and no degradation during a 5-minute 1k QPS burst. Also must pass their security checklist.
[02:24] Leah Kim: p95 600ms for 256 tokens is ambitious on some model families; we can propose quantized variants or split workloads. We'll include that in the benchmark matrix.
[02:33] Samantha Li: On security, we need SOC2 documentation, KMS integration (we use AWS KMS), and VPC peering. Also audit logs retained for 90 days — is that configurable?
[02:44] Marcus Ortega: Yes, in Dedicated/Private deployments we surface audit logs and retention config. For Hosted, we can provide export hooks but the retention policy is set by plan. We'll note that in the security doc pack.
[02:56] Daniel Cho: Can you walk through the benchmark plan? What tests?
[02:59] Jordan Patel: We'll run a 3-phase plan: steady-state (60–120 QPS for 30m), burst tests (ramp to 1.2k QPS for rolling 5m windows), and long-tail tests (simulate 95/99 token lengths and multi-turn). We'll capture p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, queue lengths, and token-cost breakdown.
[03:19] Leah Kim: We'll also instrument KV/prefix cache to show wins on repeated prefixes in the dataset. Marcus will run runs with and without caching.
[03:27] Marcus Ortega: Yes, and we'll try two model profiles: 1) a lower-latency quantized 7B with 4-bit and 2) larger 13B slightly more expensive but better quality. We'll measure per-token cost delta and p95 latency.
[03:40] Priya Rao: Quality matters — if 7B fails the acceptance test (ROUGE/semantic sim threshold on sample prompts) we won't accept it even if it's cheaper.
[03:49] Jordan Patel: Understood — we'll include a small quality eval harness using your 50 representative prompts.
[03:55] Daniel Cho: About connectivity — VPC peering + private link will be our preference if we go private. How fast can you stand up a Private edge for testing?
[04:05] Marcus Ortega: For a Private deployment we usually need network setup, certs and KMS access. Once those are in place, we can run an internal smoke bench in 48–72 hours. If you want Dedicated in our hosted cloud, we can spin benches faster, but it won't meet your KMS requirement.
[04:20] Samantha Li: AWS KMS is required — we can't hand over key material. Can you support external key wrap?
[04:25] Leah Kim: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in Private. For Dedicated we have options depending on contract. We'll document specifics.
[04:33] Priya Rao: Back to traffic shapes — we have nightly re-index jobs that fan out and create 10–15 minute tails. Do you have recommendations to absorb those without huge cost?
[04:44] Marcus Ortega: Two common patterns: 1) schedule batching to avoid coinciding peaks, and 2) use buffer + async workers so UI doesn't block on generation. On the infra side, autoscaling config and burst credit helps. We'll include autoscaling guidelines tuned to your qps burst profile.
[04:59] Daniel Cho: For the POC, we need to show end-to-end: model serving, latency telemetry in your console, and token-level cost estimates. Also want to capture traces for a few failing cases.
[05:10] Jordan Patel: We'll provide a dashboard export and a simple tracing hook you can drop into your app. Marcus: any gotchas on token counting?
[05:17] Marcus Ortega: Tokenization differences can cause mismatch. We'll standardize on the tokenizer used in the model and provide a token histogram tool. That's why we asked for sample prompts.
[05:26] Priya Rao: We'll send the sample prompt set — 75 initial prompts covering short notes, long case narratives, and multi-turn billing QAs. We'll anonymize PII.
[05:35] Samantha Li: Note: anonymization must be strong; we'll supply regex rules for redaction.
[05:39] Jordan Patel: Perfect. Timeline — we propose a 3-week pilot: week 1 gather data & env setup, week 2 run benchmarks and initial tuning, week 3 validation, handoff and recommendations. Is that ok?
[05:51] Priya Rao: Yes, that timeline works if we move quickly on logs and KMS setup.
[05:57] Leah Kim: For benchmarks we'll record: 1) Steady-state test (90 QPS for 30m), 2) Burst test (ramp to 1.2k QPS for repeated 5m windows), 3) Long-tail test (simulate 95/99 token lengths and multi-turn). Also A/B of quantization.
[06:12] Daniel Cho: One operational question: if we see p95 spikes during bursts, what's the fallback? Can Redwood route to a smaller cheaper model or queue?
[06:20] Marcus Ortega: Yes, we can configure fallback policies — serve a smaller model for best-effort or switch to cached summaries for repeated content. We can also configure rate-limited queuing with graceful degradation.
[06:31] Priya Rao: Graceful degradation is important — UX wants partial responses rather than hard errors.
[06:35] Leah Kim: We'll test partial decode behavior and streaming. Streaming reduces perceived latency; we'll demo that in week 2.
[06:43] Jordan Patel: Anything else on the metrics we should capture?
[06:46] Daniel Cho: Please capture token-level cost, GPU utilization per host, queue lengths, request shapes, and trace ids for slow requests. Also correlation between input token length and latency.
[06:58] Marcus Ortega: We'll include all of that in the bench outputs. We'll share a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens for each model/config.
[07:07] Samantha Li: For legal/procurement, we need the data flow diagram and contract SLAs draft — can you attach the standard SOC2 and data processing addendum?
[07:15] Jordan Patel: We'll include those in the security packet. I'll make sure legal sees the DPA and SOC2 letter.
[07:22] Priya Rao: One more question — do you support call-level idempotency or dedupe? We sometimes retry and that skews cost.
[07:29] Leah Kim: We recommend idempotency keys at the app layer and Redwood honors idempotency headers for a configured TTL. We'll include guidance.
[07:36] Daniel Cho: Great. On models, can you give rough cost delta between 7B quantized and 13B fp16?
[07:42] Marcus Ortega: Rough back-of-envelope: 7B 4-bit can be ~30–40% lower per-token compute cost, but quality delta depends on prompt set. We'll quantify during bench.
[07:53] Jordan Patel: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:56] Jordan Patel: Action items: Jordan will send bench plan and sheet; Leah will propose model combos and perf knobs; Marcus will run initial internal smoke tests once logs are available; Daniel to share token histograms and anonymized prompts; Samantha to confirm KMS vendor and SOC2 scope.
[08:14] Priya Rao: We'll aim to deliver logs and prompts by 2026-03-09.
[08:19] Samantha Li: Security review meeting 2026-03-11 works for us.
[08:23] Jordan Patel: Great. Anything else before we wrap?
[08:26] Daniel Cho: One last ask — can you include a section in the bench sheet for cost projection at various run rates so procurement can model monthly spend?
[08:33] Jordan Patel: Yes we'll add a run-rate cost projection table.
[08:36] Priya Rao: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the results.
[08:40] Jordan Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and benchmark plan.

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced:
- Benchmark plan (to be shared)
- Prompt sample template (customer to provide)
- Security packet: SOC2, DPA, KMS integration notes
- Shared spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens

POC acceptance criteria (agreed):
- p95 generation latency <= 600ms for <=256 output tokens on target model/config in steady-state and during controlled bursts
- Cost projection within RFP threshold for 1M tokens/month run-rate
- No SLO violations during a 5-minute 1k QPS simulated burst (no more than 5% error rate)
- Security requirements: AWS KMS integration, audit logging 90d, SOC2 evidence provided

Estimated timeline:
- 2026-03-06: Redwood shares bench plan & spreadsheet
- 2026-03-09: Alpine shares prompts and anonymized logs
- 2026-03-11: Security connectivity review
- 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-19: Bench runs and tuning
- 2026-03-20: Results review and recommendations
